text:
Some dogs sleeping at night

must dream of bones

and I remember your bones

in the flesh

or better

in that dark green dress

and those high-heeled

black, shining shoes,

you always swore when

you were drunk,

your hair slipped from your ear

you wanted to explode

from what had trapped you:

rotten memories of a

rotten

past, and

in the end

you escaped

by dying,

leaving me with the

rotten

present.

You have been dead 28 years

and still I remember you

better than any

of the others

you were the only one

who understood

the futility of the

arrangement with life.

The others were only

uncomfortable with

trivial segments,

absurdly

criticized

the little things:

Jane, you

were murdered for knowing

too much.

Here is a drink

to your bones

that

this old dog

still

dreams of.

translation.title: Some Dogs Sleeping at Night...
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The ellipsis in the supplied title and the poem's spare lineation are retained.
